newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt mkts end mostly firmer, NZD nerves persist.
newsitem.headline: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt mkts end mostly firmer, NZD nerves persist.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (SEP) 92.29 (PREV 92.28) 90-DAYS 8.18 (PREV 8.30)

* NZ short end rally subsides towards close
* Nerves about kiwi dollar persist
* Some players absent. Is rugby more important than debt?

New Zealand debt markets closed the week mostly firmer on Friday, buoyed by a bounce in the kiwi dollar, but the money market remained nervous about the currency and dealers were loath to predict lower rates.

"I think a lot of people have realised that this is probably a bit of a suckers' rally. People are very apprehensive about the currency and I think that there's still interest our there to sell any rallies," said one bill trader.
The key 90-day rate rallied down to 8.15 percent in early trade as the kiwi surged above US$0.6550 and its Trade-Weighted Index hit 65.20.

But the rally began to subside as the currency came off the boil, the 90-day at 8.18 percent for a 12-point gain on the day. "My view is we've just seen a bit of a short covering rally here and it's probably technically good levels to get in and get short again," said the trader.
Of the kiwi he said, "We've seen a bit of a short squeeze in the last two days, a bit of consolidation, but we're still hearing that big U.S. funds have interest out there to sell.
"The bear trend will continue," he added.
Mid-dated bonds took some heart from the short end's rally, the 02/01 bond yield ending a couple of pips lower at 6.95 percent.
But the long end of the yield curve rose a touch on local selling of long bonds in an otherwise very quiet session.
"I think globally you could easily see a little bit of weakness in the next few days, but overall I think the U.S. has probably still got a bit more of a rally left in it," said a senior bond dealer.
"I think we're really just going to get stuck in a range, say 6.65-95 percent (in the 11/06s).
"But today's been really quiet. After a volatile week the market's having an informal rest day I guess."

More than a few debt market dealers with an interest in rugby are reported to have thrown the "I'm sick" dummy of late, strangely coinciding with the run-up to Saturday night's giant clash between the All Blacks and the Wallabies in Melbourne.
